content: Classic (non-module, non-async, non-defer) <script src> tags execute in document order and block parsing until each loads+runs. Top-level function declarations in each classic script attach to the shared global (window) scope. Because JS is late-bound, once ALL script files have loaded, all functions can see and call each other regardless of original file order — a function in main.js can call a function defined in tabs/watchlist.js loaded after it, as long as the call happens at event-handler time (e.g. onclick), not at top-level synchronous execution time during script load. This confirms D-01's classic-script multi-file split is safe: order files logically (api.js, components/*.js, tabs/*.js, main.js) but onclick-handler references across files resolve fine since onclick fires after all scripts have loaded.
